name: Zimbabwe
summary: Victoria Falls on one border, Great Zimbabwe's stone city in the interior, Hwange's elephant herds and Mana Pools — the park where the walking safari was refined into an art.

entries.caption: Great Zimbabwe and the Zambezi
entries.description: A stone city built without mortar, and the largest sheet of falling water on earth.
entries.subject: the stone walls of Great Zimbabwe

entries.caption: Highveld and Escarpment
entries.description: Granite kopjes across the highveld, and the Zambezi escarpment dropping into the valley.
entries.subject: balancing granite boulders on the Zimbabwean highveld

entries.caption: Hwange's Elephant
entries.description: Forty thousand elephant in Hwange, drinking at pumped pans through the dry season.
entries.subject: elephants crowding a pumped waterhole in Hwange

entries.caption: Mana Pools on Foot
entries.description: The park where you may walk unguided, and where the elephant stand on their hind legs.
entries.subject: an elephant reaching into an albida tree at Mana Pools

entries.caption: The Eastern Highlands
entries.description: Nyanga, Vumba and Chimanimani along the Mozambique border, up to 2,592 metres.
entries.subject: the green Eastern Highlands at Nyanga

entries.caption: Victoria Falls
entries.description: Mosi-oa-Tunya — a mile and a half wide, and a hundred metres down, in full flood.
entries.subject: Victoria Falls in full flood with spray rising

entries.caption: The Zambezi and Kariba
entries.description: The Zambezi above the falls, and Kariba's drowned forest downstream of them.
entries.subject: dead trees standing in Lake Kariba at sunset

entries.caption: Landlocked
entries.description: No coast — the water here is the Zambezi, Kariba, and the pools of the Mana floodplain.
entries.subject: the Zambezi river wide and slow above the falls

entries.caption: Msasa and Miombo
entries.description: Miombo woodland across the country, and msasa that comes into red leaf in September.
entries.subject: msasa trees in red new leaf in September

entries.caption: Walking, Canoeing, Rafting
entries.description: Canoe the Zambezi past hippo, raft the gorge below the falls, and walk Mana with a guide.
entries.subject: canoes on the Zambezi below Mana Pools

entries.caption: Shona and Ndebele
entries.description: Shona across the centre and east, Ndebele in the west, and stone sculpture from both.
entries.subject: a Shona stone sculptor at work

entries.caption: The Stone Sculptors
entries.description: Zimbabwean stone sculpture is the country's clearest contemporary export.
entries.subject: finished stone sculptures in a Zimbabwean workshop

entries.caption: Sadza and Braai
entries.description: Sadza with relish, and meat over coals wherever there is a fire and company.
entries.subject: sadza and relish served at a Zimbabwean table

entries.caption: HIFA and the Harvest
entries.description: The Harare arts festival, and the harvest ceremonies that still open the season.
entries.subject: a performance at an arts festival in Harare

entries.caption: Stone, Basket and Wire
entries.description: Serpentine carving, Binga basketry, and wire sculpture sold on every roadside.
entries.subject: woven Binga baskets from the Zambezi valley

entries.caption: Great Zimbabwe
entries.description: Eight hundred years old, mortarless, and the largest stone structure south of the Sahara.
entries.subject: the conical tower inside the Great Enclosure

entries.caption: Khami and Matobo
entries.description: Khami's terraces, and the Matobo hills where Mzilikazi and Rhodes are both buried.
entries.subject: balancing rocks and rock art in the Matobo hills

entries.caption: Harare and Bulawayo
entries.description: Harare on the highveld, and Bulawayo's wide colonial grid built for turning an ox wagon.
entries.subject: the wide colonial streets of Bulawayo

entries.caption: Dry Stone
entries.description: Great Zimbabwe's coursed granite is the architecture, and nothing since has matched it.
entries.subject: coursed dry stone walling at Great Zimbabwe

entries.caption: Kombis and Musika
entries.description: The country runs on kombis and market days, both of which are worth an afternoon.
entries.subject: a busy produce market in a Zimbabwean town

entries.caption: Falls and Elephant
entries.description: Victoria Falls, a steam train, and elephant at a waterhole — a good week for children.
entries.subject: a family watching elephants from a Hwange hide

entries.caption: Raft, Canoe, Walk
entries.description: Grade five rafting below the falls, multi-day canoe trails, and walking safaris in Mana.
entries.subject: rafts in the Batoka gorge below Victoria Falls

entries.caption: The Old Safari Standard
entries.description: Small owner-run camps in Mana and Hwange, run by guides with the country's toughest licence.
entries.subject: a tented camp on the Zambezi floodplain at dusk

entries.caption: CAMPFIRE
entries.description: The community wildlife programme that much of the region's conservation policy was built on.
entries.subject: a community conservation meeting beside a wildlife area

entries.caption: Albida Light
entries.description: The winterthorn cathedrals of Mana Pools, in dust and low sun, are photographed everywhere.
entries.subject: dust and low sun through winterthorn trees at Mana Pools

entries.caption: Chimanimani
entries.description: A mountain range on the Mozambique border that you walk into and camp in.
entries.subject: the Chimanimani mountains on the Mozambique border

entries.caption: Guides, and Great Ruins
entries.description: The hardest guiding exam in Africa, and a stone city most visitors have never heard of.
entries.subject: a professional guide leading walkers through Mana Pools
